Opposite Party :- State Of U.P And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Alok Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Maimoona Fatima,Sheikh Moazzam Inam Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State and learned counsel appearing on behalf of the first informant.

By means of this second bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant-Sahil @ Salauddin,
who is involved in Case Crime No. 324 of 2019, under sections 376, 452 IPC, Sections 3/4 POCSO Act and Section 3 (2) 5 of S.C./S.T. Act, Police Station- Loni Border, District- Ghaziabad, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.
The first bail application of the applicant was dismissed vide order dated 04.12.2021 for want of prosecution.

As per prosecution case, in brief, informant who is father of the victim has lodged an F.I.R. on 15.04.2019 against Sahil @ Salauddin (present applicant) with the allegation inter-alia that on 15.04.2019 he, his son Rajiv and his wife had gone to factory for work.

At about 2:30 o'clock, he received an information from his neighbour that one person has barged into his house with a view to Sahil @ Salauddin vs State Of U.P And 3 Others on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157905407/
1 commit theft.

sentences.text: On the said information, he rushed to his house and saw that his daughter, aged 17 years, was with the applicant in a naked condition.
The accused-applicant was apprehended at the spot and on making query to his daughter, she told him that he committed misdeed with her.
Thereafter, he was taken to the police station.

The main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that victim was consenting party with the applicant and she herself had called the applicant to her house, where applicant was apprehended by her parents.
Much emphasis has been given by contending that it is not a case of rape but a case of consensual relationship between the applicant and victim.
Applicant has no criminal history to his credit and is languishing in jail since 16.04.2019.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that victim is minor girl and the applicant was apprehended at spot.
Victim, during the investigation as well as before the trial court, has made allegation of rape against the present applicant.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that in the present case, there is no dispute that applicant was apprehended at the spot and he was taken to the police station by the parents of the victim.

The informant and victim both were examined before the trial court as PW-1 and PW-2 but they have supported the prosecution case making allegation of rape against the applicant, therefore, as on the date, I do not find any good ground to presume the false implication of the applicant and to disbelieve the statement of the victim.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the submissions advanced on behalf of parties, gravity of offence, role assigned to applicant and severity of punishment, I do not find any good ground to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is rejected at this stage.
It is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.
